text:
I now have 70 Peruvian soles.

I take the next-to-last coin, the one that rings

69 Punic times.

And here it is, at the end of its role,

burning itself all over and blazing,

                                                    blazing,

round between my hallucinated eardrums.


It, being 69, strikes against 70;

then climbs 71, rebounds on 72.

And so it multiplies and mirrors itself undaunted

in all the other pinions.


It, vibrating and struggling,

letting out shouuutss,

releasing arduous, crackling silences,

pissing itself with natural greatness,

in unanimous rising posts,

ends up being all the numerals,

                                                the whole of life.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem XLVIII - I Now Have 70 Peruvian Soles
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the coin's arithmetic hallucination, repeated blazing, stretched shout, and bodily comedy.
